comment: kiln.npcai: the game's faction relation leaves (keen::FactionType, one byte per entity in its Faction component). Hostile(Faction*, Faction*) and its by-value twin answer 'does a fight b' (enemy targeting's candidate check 0x13c9e0 calls Hostile, so do the sensors); Friend(Faction*, Faction*[, opt]) and its by-value twin answer 'is b on a's side'. Equal factions and the players' side {Player 7, AutomatedPlayer 8, PlayerAlly 11} are friends; Hostile has the species exceptions (Vukah and WildBeast, Skeleton and Fogger, Cyclops and Wildlife ...). Leaves with no .pdata: inline hooks at their first instruction. Evidence: docs/re/npc-internals.md 3.1 and 3.6 (svn 1287369).

npcai/FactionHostile.comment: bool(const Faction* a, const Faction* b): a would fight b. 6 callers, among them enemy_combat_targets' candidate filter

npcai/FactionHostileValue.comment: bool(FactionType a, FactionType b): the same answer by value (cl, dl). 3 callers

npcai/FactionFriend.comment: bool(const Faction* a, const Faction* b): b is on a's side (equal, or both on the players' side). 1 caller

npcai/FactionFriendOpt.comment: bool(const Faction* a, const Faction* b, const Options* o): the same, plus FarmAnimal (12) on the players' side when o->[1] is set. 6 callers (the sensors among them)

npcai/FactionFriendValue.comment: bool(FactionType a, FactionType b): FactionFriend by value. 3 callers
